title: Review of c06's yeff response: on fresh seed 5 mean yield rises against the marker and giants take over, but dying cells still decline in yield (0.993 -> 0.952)
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged on fresh seed 5: c06's genealogy.py to t=50000 and a labkit pack (200 frames x 250 steps). Mean yield of particles in cells vs the inert marker: t=20000 1.060 / 0.992, t=30000 1.090 / 0.988, t=40000 1.188 / 1.007, t=50000 1.235 / 1.008, with cells 24 -> 25 -> 18 -> 9; the particles sheet shows a few cells growing into giants after t~30000, as c06 reports. abslife.py: dying mature cells go 0.993 -> 0.952 from birth to death (population 1.008 -> 1.063), 70% declined (n=20), so on this seed there is still some within-cell erosion, smaller than with a cost (about -0.04 vs -0.2) but not zero, unlike c06's 1.003 -> 1.007/1.011. birthfate.py: death share low-born 0.62 vs high-born 0.54 (marker 0.50 vs 0.64).

observations.H: data/yield_vs_marker_s5.txt: mean yield 1.09 vs marker 0.99 at t=30000 and 1.235 vs 1.008 at t=50000; rerun/seed5/particles.png giants after t~30000

seeds_run.result: response and giant takeover replicate; 'no within-cell erosion' does not (dying cells 0.993 -> 0.952, 70% declined)

controls_run.H: inert marker zm in the same run (data/yield_vs_marker_s5.txt)

verdicts.limitation: The population response replicates, but the finding's first claim (yield neutral inside a cell, no erosion, cells keep their yield for life) does not hold on this seed: 14 of 20 dying cells declined, mean -0.04. Kind at birth hardly predicts death here (0.62 vs 0.54). The response runs away into giant cells, so this regime does not keep a population of discrete cells. One seed, n=20 dying cells.
